brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Three base cells: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full and piece:0,1,0;half-n. They are joined by joint bolts at 0#0,0#0, 0#0,0#5 and 0#0,1#1, and every open side edge is finished with caps (9).

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 are 3-compartment trays. They drop in and hang on the cell rim with no fixings, so they lift out. The top covers on these cells act as lids, so a cover has to come off before its bin can be lifted out.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base at 0,1.
handle:0,0,0;top is fixed with 3 inserts to the top cover at 0,0. Handle strength and load were not checked.
check_build returned ok with no issues, and the mesh-collision check read "clear".

finish.summary: A small 3-cell portable organizer (about 25 parts) with two lift-out 3-compartment bins, one drawer, top covers, a carry handle and caps on all open edges. All configurator checks passed and the mesh-collision check is clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
